nodes.summary: Let $n$ be an even squarefree natural number with at least three prime factors, let $P$ be its largest prime factor and $d = n / P$, and let $g(n)$ be the length of the longest arithmetic progression in the absolute least reduced residue system modulo $n$. Then $\lfloor P - 2P/d \rfloor \le g(n) \le P - 1$, and if $d \ge 2P$ then $g(n) = P - 1$.
nodes.title: Longest progressions of absolute least residues: even squarefree, three or more primes

nodes.summary: The length $g(5)$ of the longest arithmetic progression in the absolute least reduced residue system modulo $5$ is $2$.
nodes.title: Longest progressions of absolute least residues modulo 5

nodes.summary: Let $n > 1$ be an odd squarefree natural number that is not prime, let $P$ be its largest prime factor and $d = n / P$, and let $g(n)$ be the length of the longest arithmetic progression in the absolute least reduced residue system modulo $n$. Then $g(n) = \lfloor P - (P + 1)/(2d) \rfloor$.
nodes.title: Longest progressions of absolute least residues: odd squarefree composite moduli

nodes.summary: Let $n > 1$ be a natural number that is neither squarefree nor a prime power, let $\operatorname{rad}(n)$ be the product of the distinct primes dividing $n$ and $P$ the largest prime factor of $n$, and let $g(n)$ be the length of the longest arithmetic progression in the absolute least reduced residue system modulo $n$. Then $g(n) = \max(n / \operatorname{rad}(n), P - 1)$.
nodes.title: Longest progressions of absolute least residues: neither squarefree nor prime power

nodes.summary: For a prime $p \equiv 3 \pmod 4$, the length $g(p)$ of the longest arithmetic progression in the absolute least reduced residue system modulo $p$ is $(p + 1)/2$.
nodes.title: Longest progressions of absolute least residues: primes congruent to 3 mod 4

nodes.summary: For a prime $p \equiv 1 \pmod 4$, the length $g(p)$ of the longest arithmetic progression in the absolute least reduced residue system modulo $p$ is $(p - 1)/2$.
nodes.title: Longest progressions of absolute least residues: primes congruent to 1 mod 4

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and $r \ge 1$, with $r \ge 2$ when $p$ is odd. Then the length $g(p^r)$ of the longest arithmetic progression in the absolute least reduced residue system modulo $p^r$ is $p^{r-1}$.
nodes.title: Longest progressions of absolute least residues: prime powers

nodes.summary: For an odd prime $p$, the length $g(2p)$ of the longest arithmetic progression in the absolute least reduced residue system modulo $2p$ is $p - 1$.
nodes.title: Longest progressions of absolute least residues: twice an odd prime

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, let $R(n)$ be the set of integers $a$ with $1 - \lceil n/2 \rceil \le a \le n - \lceil n/2 \rceil$ and $\gcd(a, n) = 1$, the system of absolute least reduced residues modulo $n$. Then $g(n)$ is the largest $s \ge 0$ for which there are an integer $b$ and a positive integer $d$ with $b + i d \in R(n)$ for every $0 \le i < s$: the length of the longest arithmetic progression with positive…
nodes.title: Longest progression in the absolute least reduced residues

nodes.summary: Let $m$ be an integer and $n$ a natural number, and let $R_m(n)$ be the set of integers $a$ with $m + 1 \le a \le m + n$ and $\gcd(a, n) = 1$. If $b$ is an integer, $d$ a positive integer and $s$ a natural number such that $b + i d \in R_m(n)$ for every $0 \le i < s$, then $s \le n$.
nodes.title: Length bound for progressions in a reduced residue window

nodes.summary: Let $n > 1$ be a natural number that is not squarefree, $\operatorname{rad}(n)$ the product of its distinct prime factors and $\operatorname{gpf}(n)$ its largest prime factor, and suppose that $\operatorname{gpf}(n) - 1 \le n / \operatorname{rad}(n)$. For an integer $m$ let $f_m(n)$ be the length of the longest arithmetic progression with positive common difference contained in the set $R_m(n)$ of integers $a$ with…
nodes.title: Average longest progression length for non-squarefree moduli

nodes.summary: Let $n > 1$ be a natural number, $\operatorname{rad}(n)$ the product of its distinct prime factors and $\operatorname{gpf}(n)$ its largest prime factor. For an integer $m$ let $f_m(n)$ be the length of the longest arithmetic progression with positive common difference contained in the set $R_m(n)$ of integers $a$ with $m + 1 \le a \le m + n$ and $\gcd(a, n) = 1$. Then the largest value of $f_m(n)$ over all integers…
nodes.title: Maximum longest progression length over all reduced residue windows

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime with $p \equiv 3 \pmod 4$. For an integer $m$ let $f_m(p)$ be the length of the longest arithmetic progression with positive common difference contained in the set $R_m(p)$ of integers $a$ with $m + 1 \le a \le m + p$ and $\gcd(a, p) = 1$. Then the least value of $f_m(p)$ over all integers $m$ is $(p + 1) / 2$.
nodes.title: Minimum longest progression length modulo a prime $p \equiv 3 \pmod 4$

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime with $p \equiv 1 \pmod 4$. For an integer $m$ let $f_m(p)$ be the length of the longest arithmetic progression with positive common difference contained in the set $R_m(p)$ of integers $a$ with $m + 1 \le a \le m + p$ and $\gcd(a, p) = 1$. Then the least value of $f_m(p)$ over all integers $m$ is $(p - 1) / 2$.
nodes.title: Minimum longest progression length modulo a prime $p \equiv 1 \pmod 4$

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and $r > 1$ a natural number. For an integer $m$ let $f_m(p^r)$ be the length of the longest arithmetic progression with positive common difference contained in the set $R_m(p^r)$ of integers $a$ with $m + 1 \le a \le m + p^r$ and $\gcd(a, p^r) = 1$. Then the least value of $f_m(p^r)$ over all integers $m$ is $p^{r-1}$.
nodes.title: Minimum longest progression length modulo a prime power

nodes.summary: For every integer $m$ and natural number $n$, $f_m(n) \le n$, where $f_m(n)$ is the length of the longest arithmetic progression with positive common difference contained in the set $R_m(n)$ of integers $a$ with $m + 1 \le a \le m + n$ and $\gcd(a, n) = 1$.
nodes.title: The longest progression length is at most the modulus

nodes.summary: Let $n > 1$ be a natural number that is neither squarefree nor a prime power, $\operatorname{rad}(n)$ the product of its distinct prime factors and $\operatorname{gpf}(n)$ its largest prime factor. For an integer $m$ let $f_m(n)$ be the length of the longest arithmetic progression with positive common difference contained in the set $R_m(n)$ of integers $a$ with $m + 1 \le a \le m + n$ and $\gcd(a, n) = 1$. nodes.title: Minimum longest progression length when $n$ is neither squarefree nor a prime power

nodes.summary: Let $m$ be an integer, $n > 1$ a squarefree natural number with largest prime factor $\operatorname{gpf}(n)$, and $d > 0$ a natural number. Then $f_m(d, n) \le \operatorname{gpf}(n) - 1$, where $f_m(d, n)$ is the length of the longest arithmetic progression with common difference $d$ contained in the set $R_m(n)$ of integers $a$ with $m + 1 \le a \le m + n$ and $\gcd(a, n) = 1$.
nodes.title: Squarefree bound for progressions with a fixed difference

nodes.summary: Let $m$ be an integer, $n > 1$ and $d > 0$ natural numbers, and $p$ a prime that divides $n$ but not $d$. Then $f_m(d, n) \le p - 1$, where $f_m(d, n)$ is the length of the longest arithmetic progression with common difference $d$ contained in the set $R_m(n)$ of integers $a$ with $m + 1 \le a \le m + n$ and $\gcd(a, n) = 1$.
nodes.title: Prime bound for progressions with a fixed difference

nodes.summary: For an integer $m$ and natural numbers $n$ and $d$, let $R_m(n)$ be the set of integers $a$ with $m + 1 \le a \le m + n$ and $\gcd(a, n) = 1$. Then $f_m(d, n)$ is the supremum of the natural numbers $s$ for which some integer $b$ has $b + i d \in R_m(n)$ for every natural number $i < s$. For $d > 0$ every such $s$ is at most $n$, so $f_m(d, n)$ is the length of the longest arithmetic progression with common…
nodes.title: Longest progression with a given common difference

nodes.summary: For an integer $m$ and a natural number $n$, let $R_m(n)$ be the reduced residue system of the integers $a$ with $m + 1 \le a \le m + n$ and $\gcd(a, n) = 1$. Then $f_m(n)$ is the largest natural number $s$ for which there are an integer $b$ and a positive integer $d$ such that $b, b + d, \dots, b + (s - 1)d$ all lie in $R_m(n)$. So it is the length of the longest arithmetic progression with positive common…
nodes.title: Length of the longest arithmetic progression in a reduced residue system

nodes.summary: The reduced residue system $R_{-3}(5)$ of the integers $a$ with $-2 \le a \le 2$ and $\gcd(a, 5) = 1$ is $\{-2, -1, 1, 2\}$: an integer $a$ lies in $R_{-3}(5)$ if and only if $a$ is one of $-2$, $-1$, $1$, $2$.
nodes.title: The reduced residue system $R_{-3}(5)$

nodes.summary: For an integer $m$ and a natural number $n$, the reduced residue system $R_m(n)$ modulo $n$ is the finite set $R_m(n) = \{a \in \mathbb{Z} : m + 1 \le a \le m + n,\ \gcd(a, n) = 1\}$.
nodes.title: The reduced residue system $R_m(n)$

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
